sources.title: VoiceOver User Guide for Mac: Use VoiceOver to navigate webpage tables
sources.version: macOS 27 (per the /mac/27 URL path and the guide's version picker)
sections: Turn grouping on or off for the current table

classes.rule: The NVDA key is insert or numpadInsert by default (capsLock can be added), and every NVDA+<key> command normalises to SRKEY+<key>, which the app never binds.
In browse mode each listed key jumps to the next element and adding shift jumps to the previous one; NVDA+shift+space switches them off or on per document.
Within a table, control+alt with arrows, home, end, pageUp or pageDown moves by cell and NVDA+control+alt+arrows reads a row or column.
Control stops speech, shift pauses it and Control+alt+n starts NVDA, while the desktop layout also uses bare numpad keys for review and mouse (no row: outside the app's key vocabulary).

NVDA+space toggles browse and focus mode, escape returns to browse mode after an automatic switch, enter or space enter focus mode on controls that need it, and NVDA+control+space leaves an embedded object.
JAWS commands pair INSERT (desktop layout) or CAPS LOCK (laptop layout) with other keys and normalise to SRKEY+<key>, which the app never binds.
Navigation Quick Keys act in the Virtual Cursor, holding SHIFT moves to the previous instance, and CTRL+INSERT with a starred key lists those elements.
ALT+CTRL+arrows move cell by cell and WINDOWS KEY+ALT+arrows move by row or column, with the Windows key normalised as the token Win placed first.
CTRL interrupts speech, ALT+CTRL+PAGE UP or PAGE DOWN changes the rate, CTRL+SHIFT+brackets set frames, and arrows plus PAGE UP or PAGE DOWN steer Say All.
Layered commands start with INSERT+SPACEBAR (laptop CAPS LOCK+SPACEBAR) and JAWS takes the following key or keys.
examples: INSERT+SPACEBAR, followed by T, and then QUESTION MARK

classes.rule: Desktop-layout numpad keys and many WINDOWS Key combinations are JAWS commands; norms use DOM code names (NumpadAdd, Numpad5) and the token Win, outside the app's key vocabulary.
ENTER turns Forms Mode on, NUM PAD PLUS turns it off, and INSERT+Z toggles the Virtual PC Cursor.

VO is Control-Option or Caps Lock (both by default), every VO-<key> command normalises to Ctrl+Alt+<key>, and VO-Command-<key> folds to the same norm because Command maps to Ctrl. Optional extra VO modifiers can be switched on in VoiceOver Utility (Commands > 'Also control VoiceOver with'): the Option key (the right Option key by default when enabled; norm Alt) and the numeric keypad; they are off unless the user enables them.

Single-key Quick Nav works only after VO-Q turns it on; the guide shows just b/B and 1/! and leaves the full default list to VoiceOver Utility, and the fetched pages do not state the default on/off state.
Table commands are VO combinations: VO-R and VO-C read headers, VO-Shift-T gives the position, VO-Command-Y moves by column (ungrouped) and VO-Home/VO-End reach cells (grouped).
Command-F5 toggles VoiceOver anywhere, and Escape (or Fn-Tab) closes VoiceOver menus or the rotor and leaves VoiceOver modes.

VO-Shift-Down/Up Arrow start and stop interacting, VO-Q and VO-Shift-Q toggle single-key and arrow-key Quick Nav, and arrow-key Quick Nav also uses arrow pairs pressed together (no norm: not expressible).
